title: The Farmer, the Sage and the Hidden Treasure
director: claude-opus-5-5 (authored in Claude Code, same rules as scripts/audio/direct.ts)

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [warmly] Welcome to LitBridge, where stories cross languages. Today's story comes from the Hindi tradition. It is a village tale, passed from grandparent to grandchild along the Ganga. It is called... The Farmer, the Sage and the Hidden Treasure.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [amused] In a village on the banks of the Ganga lived a farmer named Ramdin, who loved his charpai more than his plough.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: His fields grew weeds taller than his children... and every year, the family ate a little less.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: One afternoon, a sage stopped under the neem tree by his house and asked for water. Ramdin brought it, and complained, as he always did.

lines.speaker: ramdin
lines.text: [grumbling] Bad luck, Maharaj. Bad luck and stingy rain. What can a poor man do?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The sage listened. Then he lowered his voice.

lines.speaker: sage
lines.text: [conspiratorial whisper] Your grandfather was a wise man. He buried his wealth in these very fields. Dig... and you will find it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [brightly] The next morning, Ramdin was in the field before the crows.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He dug the eastern corner, then the western one. His wife brought him rotis and buttermilk, and stayed to help. His sons, curious, joined in.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: For weeks they turned over every clod of earth, broke every stone, and pulled out every root.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [sighs] They found no pot of gold. Only blisters.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then the monsoon came. Ramdin, tired and embarrassed, scattered the seed he had left over the freshly dug soil, because it seemed a waste not to.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [warmly] The loosened earth drank the rain. By autumn, his wheat stood golden and heavy, higher than any in the village.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: When the sage passed that way again, Ramdin fell at his feet.

lines.speaker: ramdin
lines.text: [moved] There was no treasure, Maharaj... and yet I have never been so rich.

lines.speaker: sage
lines.text: [gently amused] There was treasure. You simply had to dig to find it. [short pause] Do it again next year.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [warmly] The treasure was the work itself, and the earth rewards those who turn it. Thank you for listening to LitBridge.
